features.title: Pair a phone over a self-provisioned HTTPS tunnel
features.summary: Opt-in public phone access with agent tools: the persisted setting decides whether DSH exposes the gateway, the tools enable, disable, print a fresh code and revoke devices, and the chosen provider provisions the tunnel (Tailscale first, public tunnel fallback). Redemption issues a persistent per-device cookie; the gateway proxies to the loopback native listener with its own exchanged cookie.
features.currentSurface: host: loopback gateway, terminal QR and the rail's Pair a phone dialog
reach: expect text "Phone access is off. Ask the agent to enable it, then open this again."
failureModes: Nothing is published until settings.json enables phone access; the disabled startup only prints the enable path and detected providers.
A missing tunnel provider or unusable native cookie reports on the terminal and never exposes the native listener.

An expired, reused, replaced, wrong or rate-limited pairing attempt is refused without issuing a device, and the phone page says which and what to do next; a phone that already paired is told so, spends no code and gets Open DSH.
A page load with a device cookie DSH no longer accepts gets a Pair this phone again page, not a bare 401.
Revocation stops new requests for that cookie but does not yet drop sockets already open.

A busy gateway port (phone-access's proxy holds 3443 by default) starts no tunnel and leaves phone access off; phone_pairing_status names the holder, the lsof command and a free port, which phone_pairing_enable accepts as port.
More than eight pending codes replace the oldest instead of failing.

With phone-access listening on a public origin, pairing claims /pair and its cookie there through phone-access's edge API and runs no tailscale command; on its own route it takes only an HTTPS port nothing serves and turns off only that port while it still points at its gateway.

externalDependencies.deterministicFake: Tunnel startup is injectable through the loopback gateway tests; no provider is invoked there.
